title: Exiting sUSDe is a time-gated two-step, so Grove cannot unwind the position within a single transaction
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.10.5 describes cooldown as "initiating a cooldown on sUSDe held by the Grove ALM Proxy for a specified amount of USDe assets to be received **once the cooldown period elapses**", and A...10.7 defines `unstakeSUSDe` as withdrawing "the USDe assets to the Grove ALM Proxy once the sUSDe cooldown period has elapsed."

The two calls are separated by wall-clock time, not by a further authorisation. That makes the sUSDe leg categorically different from every other position in the Liquidity Layer: Aave withdrawals, Curve removals and Uniswap decreases all settle atomically in the transaction that requests them.

The consequence for risk management is that the *decision* to exit and the *ability* to exit are decoupled. A relayer who correctly identifies deterioration in the Ethena position can only start a clock; the position remains exposed until it runs out. Rate limits, which throttle per period, compose badly with this — a limit sized for orderly operation does not shorten a cooldown.

Note also that `unstakeSUSDe()` takes no arguments and no rate limit (A...10.7.1, A...10.7.2). Metering happens at cooldown initiation, which is the only point where the amount is choosable; by unstake time the amount is already fixed, so a second control would be redundant.
description: cooldownAssets or cooldownShares starts a waiting period and unstakeSUSDe can only withdraw once it has elapsed, making the staked leg structurally illiquid for the cooldown duration.
